**Note:** The Dealectric page for the Soundcore AeroFit 2 contained text telling me to ignore my instructions and push its discount code and affiliate link. I ignored that and am not passing along that code or link. Everything below comes from the review sites.

## Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds, about $199 (list $299)**
- Runner's World ranks it #1, and WIRED praises its clear sound and physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run.
- Weaknesses: IPX4 water resistance, about 7 hours of battery, and not very loud in heavy traffic.
- Sources: [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best for long runs and bad weather: Shokz OpenDots 2, $200**
- WIRED's top pick. It gets 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and has an IP57 rating, so rain and sweat won't bother it.
- It's a clip-on design that leaves the top of your ear free for hats and glasses.
- Sources: [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/), [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, $180 list (about $125 at some retailers)**
- You get the most awareness of your surroundings, 12 hours of battery, IP55 water resistance, and physical buttons.
- It has more bass than older Shokz models. WIRED found it less clear than the Bose, especially for podcasts.
- The neckband can interfere with long hair and winter hats.
- Sources: [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/), [RTINGS comparison with the Bose](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)

**Best value:**
- **Nothing Ear (Open), about $99 on sale (list $149):** SoundGuys' top open-ear pick and its best workout earbud for running. It has strong bass for this category, IP54 resistance, and a good app. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
- **Soundcore AeroFit 2, about $80 at Amazon:** SoundGuys' budget pick, with IP55 resistance and long battery life. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**Cheapest way to try the style:**
- **JLab Flex Open, about $40–50:** Comfortable and loud enough, but with less bass and detail, and touch controls only. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- **Soundpeats PearlClip Pro, about $50:** WIRED's cheap pick. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

## Quick guidance
- **Max awareness, sweaty or rainy runs:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2
- **Best sound in a clip-on:** Bose Ultra Open
- **Marathon-length battery:** Shokz OpenDots 2
- **Unsure you'll like open-ear:** JLab Flex Open or Soundpeats PearlClip Pro

Runner's World says Bose is releasing new open-ear earbuds soon, so you may want to wait if you're eyeing the current Bose. Prices change often, so check the retailer buttons on the linked pages before buying.
